stories.summary: East Africa: Ghana Set to Overtake Ethiopia As Africa's Eighth-Largest Economy After Kenya Takes East Africa Lead 19 October 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Ghana is projected to overtake Ethiopia as Africa's eighth-largest economy in 2026, with its gross domestic product (GDP) forecast to reach US$128.64 billion, exceeding Ethiopia's projected US$127.15 billion by US$1.49 billion, according to the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) October 2026 World Economic Outlook (WEO), as reported by African Business Insider on 17 October. The projected shift comes after Kenya overtook Ethiopia as East Africa's largest economy in nominal US dollar terms, marking another change in the continent's economic rankings driven partly by exchange-rate movements rather than differences in real economic growth. The IMF's latest estimates place Ghana eighth among Africa's largest economies, ahead of Ethiopia in ninth place and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), whose economy is projected at US$122.28 billion. While Ghana's nominal GDP is expected to edge ahead of Ethiopia's, the two countries have markedly different growth forecasts. Ethiopia's economy is projected to expand by 9.2% in real terms in 2026, compared with Ghana's forecast growth of 5.7%.

stories.title: Kenya: Authorities Must Address Economic Grievances Driving Protests, End Repressive Tactics
stories.summary: Kenya: Authorities Must Address Economic Grievances Driving Protests, End Repressive Tactics 19 October 2026 Amnesty International (London) Kenyan authorities have increasingly used authoritarian tactics, including arbitrary arrests and detention, abductions, malicious prosecution of protesters, surveillance, and media repression, to crack down on protests against deepening economic hardship and the government's aggressive fiscal policies, Amnesty International said in a new report today. The report, " Human Rights Under Siege: Unpacking Authoritarian Practices in an Era of Economic Pressure amid Youth-Led Protests in Kenya", documents how between 2023 and 2025, increased food and transport costs, levies and tax hikes, high public debt, corruption, rising poverty and inequality, as well as broken electoral promises led to public anger and protests. "The findings of this report are troubling and paint a stark picture of the Kenyan government's repressive response to real grievances affecting the day-to-day lives of ordinary people," said George Morara, Amnesty International Kenya's Executive Director. "The state's attempts to divert attention away from its failure to address its human rights obligations have not worked. Authorities must address the economic grievances underpinning the protests, end the escalating crackdown on dissent, and ensure accountability for human rights violations during the 2023 to 2025 economic and tax related protests." According to the latest statistics from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), no fewer than 268 deaths have so far been recorded in 2026, with the case fatality rate rising to 23.6 per cent, up from 18.6 per cent during the same period in 2025. Another 15 countries have expressed intent to join the initiative, and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) is targeting all 55 African Union Member States to participate in the APPM. The announcement came at the conclusion of the third APPM Member States Consultative Workshop held in Addis Ababa, marking a shift from political commitment to implementation, in line with African Union directives. Established by an African Union Assembly decision in February 2024, the APPM is spearheaded by Africa CDC to strengthen collective purchasing of essential health products across the continent. By pooling demand from Member States, the APPM aims to improve access to affordable, quality-assured health products, strengthen supply security, reduce procurement costs and create predictable, sustainable markets for African manufacturers.

The DRC's worst-ever Ebola outbreak has now passed the 9,000-case mark, with the number of deaths topping 4,000 at the beginning of this month. Un doublé de Béni Namboka (32e, 43e) a d'abord lancé les Congolais, avant qu'Ekofo Mudiayi y aille lui aussi de son doublé (63e, 83e) pour porter le score à 4-0.

stories.title: Africa: Every Story Is Unique, Every Journey Matters for Women's Cancers
stories.summary: Africa: Every Story Is Unique, Every Journey Matters for Women's Cancers WHO-Africa Raising awareness of early detection of breast cancer, at the WHO regional office for Africa. 18 October 2026 allAfrica.com guest column By Dr Fatima Maada Bio, Ambassador Amma Twum-Amoah, and Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus Addis Ababa and Geneva — Leaders of the Organization of African First Ladies for Development, the African Union and the World Health Organization issue a call to accelerate action on women's cancers in Africa in this AllAfrica guest column during Breast Cancer Awareness Month Across Africa, too many women are dying prematurely from breast and cervical cancers. In 2024 alone, 350,000 women across the continent died from these diseases, often because prevention, early detection, diagnosis and treatment came too late or were inaccessible. Behind every statistic is a woman, a family and a community. A mother waiting too long for a diagnosis. A daughter unable to access preventive care.

stories.title: Kenya Confirms Four New Ebola Cases
stories.summary: Seven Ebola infections have now been confirmed in Kenya, which before this month had never recorded cases of the deadly virus.

stories.title: Ligue des champions CAF: Mamelodi Sundowns freiné par Wiliete, le MC Alger en danger
stories.summary: Ligue des champions CAF: Mamelodi Sundowns freiné par Wiliete, le MC Alger en danger Le Mamelodi Sundowns, champion en titre, n'a pas réussi à l'emporter (0-0) à l'extérieur contre les Angolais du Wiliete SC, ce dimanche 18 octobre, dans le match aller du dernier tour des qualifications pour la phase de groupes de la Ligue des champions. Un nul frustrant, mais pas aussi douloureux que la défaite 2-0 du MC Alger chez les Enugu Rangers, qui met en danger le dernier club algérien en lice dans la compétition. Publié le : 18/10/2026 - 19:49 Modifié le : 18/10/2026 - 22:23 2 min Temps de lecture Le Mamelodi Sundowns va devoir l'emporter au match retour à domicile contre Wiliete pour se qualifier pour la phase de groupes de la Ligue des champions. © Courtesy of CAF Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite Le match, retardé d'une demi-heure par la météo en raison de la menace d'un orage, a finalement accouché d'une partie frustrante pour les champions d'Afrique en titre, au stade National de Tundavala, à Lubango, en Angola. Le Mamelodi Sundowns n'a pas réussi à se défaire de Wiliete, au terme d'une partie qui s'est soldée sur un 0-0, malgré de grosses occasions ratée dans les 45 premières minutes. En plus d'avoir un match retour à disputer, dans lequel tout restera à faire pour se qualifier pour la phase de groupes, les Brésiliens ont perdu Teboho Mokoena sur blessure, alors même que le gardien Ronwen Williams était indisponible pour la rencontre.

stories.title: Nigeria: huit soldats tués par une mine posée par des jihadistes à la frontière avec le Cameroun
stories.summary: Nigeria: huit soldats tués par une mine posée par des jihadistes à la frontière avec le Cameroun Au Nigeria, huit militaires ont été tués, samedi 17 octobre, lorsque leur véhicule a heurté une mine posée par des jihadistes. Ce grave incident a eu lieu dans l'État de Borno, épicentre de la violence jihadiste, dans le nord-est du pays, tout près de la frontière avec le Cameroun. L'engin explosif, placé sur la route, a été déclenché à distance, selon les premières informations. Publié le : 18/10/2026 - 19:29 2 min Temps de lecture Des soldats de l'armée du Nigeria en patrouille en mars 2024. (image d'illustration) AP - Sunday Alamba Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite La mine qui a causé la mort de huit militaires nigérians et qui a blessé un membre d'une milice d'auto-défense, semble avoir été déclenchée à l'aide d'un cordon détonant. Les soldats ont été tués alors qu'ils inspectaient le travail de milices anti-jihadistes qui débroussaillaient les fourrés le long de la route d'accès à la ville de Gamboru.

stories.title: Colorfol, musique à la carte au Cameroun pour musiciens en développement
stories.summary: L'Afrique en marche Colorfol, musique à la carte au Cameroun pour musiciens en développement Publié le : 18/10/2026 - 18:12 Comment faire face aux mastodontes de la musique et des contenus que sont Spotify, Deezer ou YouTube et promouvoir la musique de son pays et des jeunes artistes qui méritent d'être entendus ? C'est le défi que s'est fixé, depuis bientôt six ans, la plateforme camerounaise Colorfol. Un petit Poucet musical qui veut devenir grand. Site Colorfol © Colorfol Publicité Créée en 2019, la plateforme d'écoute Colorfol permet aux fans de bikutsi, de makossa ou de rap camerounais de retrouver leurs musiciens préférés, et aussi et surtout de découvrir des artistes en plein développement de carrière. À Douala, Ronny Kitio, ingénieur informatique, a eu l'idée de créer cette plateforme pour rendre service au début à une amie chanteuse en mal de visibilité.

stories.title: Comment l’administration de Donald Trump utilise des pays africains pour expulser des migrants en dépit du droit international
stories.summary: Sur les 28 000 immigrés expulsés des Etats-Unis entre le début de 2025 et août 2026, plus de 500 ont été envoyés sur le continent africain, selon les données du Deportation Data Project. La plupart du temps, ils n’ont pas de lien direct avec les pays d’Afrique.

stories.title: France: Paris, Lyon and Marseille count the cost after violent protests
stories.summary: Streets littered with broken glass, burnt bicycles and debris greeted residents in France on Sunday 18 October, following demonstrations that left extensive damage across Paris, Lyon and Marseille.

stories.title: Cameroun : sur la route Douala-Yaoundé, sept heures pour parcourir 230 kilomètres
stories.summary: Cameroun : sur la route Douala-Yaoundé, sept heures pour parcourir 230 kilomètres Le délabrement de la route Douala-Yaoundé exaspère les usagers et inquiète jusqu’aux cadres du parti au pouvoir. Alors que le gouvernement annonce de nouveaux travaux, le financement et les délais de reconstruction restent des défis majeurs. Travaux d’urgence pour combler les nids-de-poule sur la route entre Yaoundé et Douala. © DR Par Franck Foute (à Yaoundé) Publié aujourd'hui à 15h55, modifié à 11h14 Lecture : 4 minutes. Ils proposent aux usagers des transports en commun reliant Douala à Yaoundé coincés dans les embouteillages de s’en extraire et de traverser la localité, moyennant 15 000 F CFA.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV thanks faithful for prayers at first appearance since surgery
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV thanked the thousands of faithful in the Vatican’s Saint Peter’s Square on Sunday for their prayers while he was hospitalised earlier this week.

stories.title: Russia: Huge flames and smoke rise over St Petersburg after drone strikes
stories.summary: Huge plumes of black smoke billowed over St Petersburg, Russia’s second-largest city, on Sunday, 18 October, as a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack sparked fires at industrial and logistics facilities. Russian officials said 126 drones had been intercepted in the surrounding region.

stories.title: Dans les archives de la poésie senghorienne, avec la chercheuse Claire Riffard
stories.summary: Envie de livres Dans les archives de la poésie senghorienne, avec la chercheuse Claire Riffard La collection « Dans l'atelier de... » du CNRS nous a fait découvrir la méthode et la magie à l'œuvre dans les travaux littéraires de quelques-unes des grands noms des lettres mondiales. Après notamment Baudelaire, Voltaire, Virginia Woolf, la série convoque archives et manuscrits pour nous faire entrer dans l'atelier du grand poète francophone Léopold Sédar Senghor. Ce livre est une invitation à découvrir et à comprendre la genèse et l'originalité de son œuvre poétique, qui fait partie aujourd'hui des grands classiques africains. Retour à l'œuvre senghorienne à travers cinq thématiques abordées par son exégète, Claire Riffard. Publié le : 18/10/2026 - 16:44 7 min Temps de lecture [Image d'illustration] Léopold Sédar Senghor, ancien président du Sénégal, académicien, poète, posant le 10 mai 1985 à Tours, lors d'un colloque consacré à son œuvre.

stories.title: Smashed storefronts, burned buildings: France wakes up to aftermath of violent protests
stories.summary: France woke up Sunday to devastated streets after clashes between police and protesters, mass looting and fires erupted nationwide as marches against rising costs of living degenerated into "extreme" violence.

stories.title: IMF annual meeting: Developing nations need greater digital connectivity
stories.summary: An AI boom is lifting technology-exporting economies. But rising energy costs and climate disasters are pushing many developing nations into debt distress. Greater digital connectivity would allow them to benefit from tech advances.

stories.title: Cameroon's opposition MRC elects its first female president, Tiriane Noah
stories.summary: Cameroon’s main opposition MRC elected a new party president on Saturday, Tiriane Balbine Noah. She replaces Maurice Kamto and becomes the first woman to lead the party.

stories.title: Togo: l'opposition et la société civile rejettent toujours tout dialogue avec le pouvoir
stories.summary: Togo: l'opposition et la société civile rejettent toujours tout dialogue avec le pouvoir Au Togo, plusieurs coalitions de partis d'opposition et d'organisations de la société civile rejettent toujours tout dialogue avec le pouvoir. Après la réforme constitutionnelle - mars 2024 - qui a changé le régime présidentiel en régime parlementaire, ces coalitions - regroupées dans le Manifeste Génération Togo - exigent la mise en place d'une période de transition. Publié le : 18/10/2026 - 14:52 Modifié le : 18/10/2026 - 14:53 2 min Temps de lecture Vue générale de Lomé, Togo © AP Lomé Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite Les protestataires s'appuient sur l'arrêt de la Cour de justice de la Cédéao, publié en janvier 2026, et qui juge Lomé coupable d'avoir procédé à un « changement anticonstitutionnel de gouvernement ». Le Manifeste Génération Togo renouvelle son refus du dialogue avec les autorités, en réaction aux déclarations du ministre des Relations avec les Institutions, Gilbert Bawara tenues, il y a une semaine. C'est en effet l'intervention de Gilbert Bawara devant le Parlement qui a poussé le Manifeste Génération Togo à réagir.

stories.title: En Ouganda, comment Muhoozi Kainerugaba étend son influence de l’armée à la politique
stories.summary: En Ouganda, comment Muhoozi Kainerugaba étend son influence de l’armée à la politique Depuis la réélection de Yoweri Museveni en janvier 2026, l’emprise du chef d’état-major de l’armée sur son pays ne cesse de croître. Du Parlement au gouvernement en passant par la sphère économique, il a continué à étendre son réseau, se positionnant plus que jamais comme le successeur de son père. Le chef d’état-major des armées ougandaises, Muhoozi Kainerugaba. © Montage JA Par Romain Gras Publié aujourd'hui à 12h15 Lecture : 8 minutes. stories.title: Cameroun : ces femmes qui font l’économie
stories.summary: Cameroun : ces femmes qui font l’économie Banque, BTP, cacao : six Camerounaises brisent les plafonds de verre et dynamisent l’économie locale. stories.title: Entre Sahara et océan, la petite ville marocaine de Lagouira attise l’intérêt de la Mauritanie
stories.summary: Entre Sahara et océan, la petite ville marocaine de Lagouira attise l’intérêt de la Mauritanie Alors que les négociations sur le Sahara occidental se poursuivent, la Mauritanie souhaite faire reconnaître sa souveraineté sur la ville marocaine de Lagouira. Éclairage historique sur un enjeu territorial majeur. Lagouira se situe à l’ouest du Ras Nouadibhou, sur une petite péninsule de quelques kilomètres de large plonge du nord au sud, coupée en deux verticalement par la frontière maroco-mauritanienne. © Michel Uyttebroeck/PiccayaADOBESTOCK Par Farid Bahri Publié aujourd'hui à 10h34 Lecture : 5 minutes. stories.title: Hilarious quips and ‘100,000-volt’ energy: the hypemen (and women) redefining Afrobeats music
stories.summary: Toby Shang, one of the leading lights of the growing Afrohype genre. Photograph: Sogo Oladele/The Guardian Style of emceeing based on high-octane, ad-libbed vocals has flourished thanks to its unique way of captivating crowds By Eromo Egbejule in Lagos F or the 2015 freshmen cohort of the history degree programme at the University of Lagos, their classmate’s first-semester presentation was so captivating that they began calling him Toby Shang, after the 16th-century Chinese dynasty he had focused on. His crowd engagement that day had been harnessed from his high school days as a ginger-man (energiser) in a three-man band and as a private tutor. By his final year at university, his viral catchphrases and infectious energy had resulted in a hit song, Shedibalabala. Today, he is one of the self-acclaimed “evangelists and pioneers” in the Afrobeats sub-genre some are now calling Afrohype or lamba.

stories.title: Nigeria's Army Chief of Staff visits troops in Borno after deaths of 15 soliders
stories.summary: The Nigerian Army Chief of Staff is visiting troops stationed in the northeast of the country, a few days after jihadists killed fifteen soldiers in the region.

stories.title: Sudanese gold miners describe deadly airstrike that killed 72
stories.summary: Sudanese miners injured in a deadly airstrike along the border with Egypt last week have been describing how the incident unfolded.

stories.title: En Tunisie, plusieurs milliers de personnes ont manifesté samedi dans les rues de la capitale, malgré la répression du régime de Kaïs Saïed
stories.summary: Depuis le coup de force du président tunisien, il y a cinq ans, une chape de plomb s’est abattue sur le pays. Une marche s’est malgré tout tenue à Tunis samedi 17 octobre, à l’appel de nombreuses organisations syndicales et de la société civile.

stories.title: An extraordinary life: descendant welcomes biography of woman ‘gifted’ to Queen Victoria
stories.summary: Sarah Forbes Bonetta was brought to England by Frederick Forbes, of the Royal Navy’s West Africa Squadron. Photograph: William Bambridge (1819-79)/Royal Collection Trust View image in fullscreen Sarah Forbes Bonetta was brought to England by Frederick Forbes, of the Royal Navy’s West Africa Squadron. Photograph: William Bambridge (1819-79)/Royal Collection Trust An extraordinary life: descendant welcomes biography of woman ‘gifted’ to Queen Victoria A girl called Àìná was captured by an African king and later taken to England to become Sarah Forbes Bonetta, protege of the imperial monarch When she was seven years old, Bayo Randle’s great-great-grandmother Sarah Forbes Bonetta was presented to Queen Victoria at Windsor Castle as a “diplomatic gift” from an African king. Victoria would go on to pay for Bonetta’s education, approve her marriage to one of west Africa’s wealthiest men, and become godmother to her eldest daughter. But while Victoria took a genuine interest in Bonetta’s welfare, making the orphan a royal protege and meeting with her over the years, their relationship was part of a bigger agenda.

stories.summary: Officials in DR Congo are accusing former president Joseph Kabila of planning a general attack on the country. Kabila on Monday joined forces with the rebel M23 to head a new outfit , taking a more direct role in the insurgency ravaging eastern DRC.

stories.summary: Le fils du chef de l’Etat, déjà à la tête des forces armées et successeur présumé de son père à la présidence, est accusé de multiples violations des droits humains et enchaîne, sur les réseaux sociaux, les tirades aussi baroques que terrifiantes.

stories.summary: The White House inquiry is focused on diverging accounts from Richard Grenell and Alina Habba Mildon about a $17 million transfer from a government account in the African country to a Texas defense firm.

stories.summary: La première dame et huit autres proches de Félix Tshisekedi sont au cœur d’une instruction pour blanchiment d’argent, ouverte par la justice belge en 2025. stories.title: Egypt's President Sisi will step down when term expires in 2030
stories.summary: Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi says he’ll leave office when his term expires in 2030. Making the announcement on Saturday, Sisi described the matter as “completely settled.”

stories.title: Frontline workers in DRC receive Ervebo vaccine amid growing Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: Frontline workers in DR Congo received the Ervebo vaccine on Friday as the country’s worst ever Ebola outbreak continues to spread. stories.summary: Course à l’hydrogène vert au Maghreb : le Maroc garde-t-il une longueur d’avance ? stories.summary: Lors du sixième tour de scrutin au sein du Conseil de sécurité, tous les candidats, dont l’ex-président sénégalais, se sont retrouvés sous la menace d’un possible veto de la part de plusieurs des cinq membres permanents.

stories.title: Lounès Magramane, un diplomate choisi pour succéder à Boualem Boualem au cabinet de la présidence algérienne
stories.summary: Lounès Magramane, un diplomate choisi pour succéder à Boualem Boualem au cabinet de la présidence algérienne Sa nomination a surpris, d’autant que lui-même se voyait plutôt ambassadeur à Paris. stories.title: Senegal's Macky Sall withdraws from race for UN top job
stories.summary: Senegal’s former President Macky Sall is pulling out of the race to lead the United Nations. Saturday's announcement comes one day after an informal straw poll by UN Security Council members saw all seven candidates receive at least one veto.

stories.title: Cameroun anglophone – Felix Agbor Balla : « Le gouvernement doit comprendre que dialoguer n’est pas une faiblesse »

stories.title: Iran denies being behind Houthi attacks as Aden airport hit
stories.summary: Iran has denied any involvement in an escalation of attacks by Houthi rebels on Saudi targets. The international airport in Yemen’s interim capital Aden was struck by two missiles late on Friday, the second such incident in less than two weeks.

stories.title: Au Mali, les dessous de la bataille pour le contrôle de la Maison de la presse
stories.summary: Alors que son second mandat touche à sa fin, Bandiougou Danté se prépare à se représenter à la présidence de la Maison de la presse. Un début de fronde s’organise contre ce proche d’Assimi Goïta, promoteur d’un « traitement patriotique de l’information ».

stories.title: Ex-fighters in Ethiopia's Tigray region register for reintegration programme
stories.summary: Hundreds of former fighters in Ethiopia’s northern Tigray region have been signing up for a government programme to help them return to civilian life.

stories.title: Morocco's King Mohammed VI formally appoints first woman-led government
stories.summary: Morocco's King Mohammed VI formally appoints the members of his country's new government, led for the first time in its history by a woman prime minister, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri.

stories.title: Patients in chains rescued from suspected illegal rehab centre in South Africa
stories.summary: Image source, Department of social development Image caption, Officials uncovered "gross inhuman conditions" when they raided the centre By Khanyisile Ngcobo Reporting from Johannesburg Published 16 October 2026 A pastor and his wife have been arrested in South Africa after 200 people, some in chains, were found held at a suspected illegal rehabilitation centre in the north-eastern part of the country. The facility, operated from a church in Mpumalanga province, was discovered during an operation by officials in the area on Thursday. Authorities said they uncovered "gross inhumane conditions" when they raided the facility, with some patients found with "sores all over their bodies" and "others chained to each other". Police have since charged the couple, who were running the facility, with kidnapping but could add more charges. Illegal rehabilitation centres have mushroomed in South Africa in recent years as drug use spirals in the country.

stories.title: The Bundestag has debated the genocide Germany carried out in Namibia a century ago. But will it spur progress on addressing colonial crimes?
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5OL1o Gaob David Timotheus Frederick (left) and Mutjinde Katjiua visited Germany this week to demand recognition and restitution Image: Christian Ditsch/epd Advertisement Gaob Daniel Timotheus Frederick was sitting in the front row of the visitors' gallery in the Bundestag this week. Wearing a suit and hat, he had traveled all the way from Namibia to see this parliamentary debate unfold. For almost 120 years, his family had been waiting for the return of human remains of their ancestor, Cornelius Frederick (sometimes spelled Fredericks), who had led the Nama resistance against German colonial rule and died on Shark Island in Germany's first concentration camp . In the name of his great-grandfather and as a member of the Nama Traditional Leaders Association (NTLA), Frederick was there to demand an "unconditioned apology" from Germany. Sitting next to him, in uniform and white gloves, with a carved lion on the handle of his walking stick, was the head of the Ovaherero Traditional Authority, Paramount Chief Mutjinde Katjiua.

stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Mauritius is a well known as a tourism and financial services hub By Basillioh Rukanga Published 14 October 2026 Updated 15 October 2026 Police in Mauritius imposed an overnight curfew overnight to quell the worst riots to break out on the Indian Ocean island in decades. Protests over water shortages and the high cost of living that started a week ago erupted into violence on Friday when a woman was shot and wounded by police at a roadblock. The circumstances of the shooting are not clear, but the officer has since been arrested and remanded in custody. Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam ordered the curfew on Tuesday, warning against those "acting against the interests of the country", which is a tourism and financial services hub. "Those who have carried out these actions will have to face the very heavy consequences warranted by their anti-patriotic acts," he said in an address to the nation. The government said it was extending the curfew until Friday morning as part of the measures agreed on during a special cabinet meeting on Wednesday.

stories.title: Ghana's Semenyo 'froze' after alleged racist abuse, court told
stories.summary: Image source, Press Association Image caption, Antoine Semenyo was playing for Bournemouth when the alleged incident happened during a match against Liverpool in August 2025 Published 14 October 2026 Footballer Antoine Semenyo "froze" after he was allegedly racially abused by a Liverpool fan during a Premier League match at Anfield, a court has heard. The Manchester City winger, who was playing for Bournemouth at the time, was preparing to take a throw-in when Mark Mogan, 47, allegedly shouted a racist insult at him on 15 August 2025. Prosecutors said Semenyo was "clearly hurt and upset" and reported the incident to referee Anthony Taylor when the ball next went out of play. Mogan, of Dovecot, Liverpool, denies racially aggravated behaviour. Liverpool Magistrates' Court heard Mogan, who uses a wheelchair, shouted an offensive slur about 30 minutes into the opening match of the Premier League season.

stories.title: Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns
stories.summary: The trial would withhold hepatitis B vaccines from thousands of newborns in a country where the disease is widespread. Photograph: Phanie/Sipa Press/Alamy View image in fullscreen The trial would withhold hepatitis B vaccines from thousands of newborns in a country where the disease is widespread. Photograph: Phanie/Sipa Press/Alamy Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK Jr Guinea-Bissau has not approved the controversial hepatitis B study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday. The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would instead track “nonspecific” health outcomes like overall mortality or neurodevelopmental conditions, has been championed by Robert F Kennedy Jr , secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime anti-vaccine activist. Members of a Danish research ethics committee were informed that officials in Guinea-Bissau had approved an updated design of the study, which influenced some committee members’ votes to proceed with the trial last week.

stories.title: From black soldier flies to mealworms: farming insects for food, fodder and fertiliser in Uganda
stories.summary: Mealworms are consumed as food in many parts of the world. Photograph: Umberto Diecinove Cultivating the nutritious bugs means families can raise livestock and enrich their own food, while lowering pressures on the land By Umberto Diecinove A few minutes’ walk from his home in the Kyaka II refugee settlement, Kanane Bikanyale feeds black soldier fly larvae to chickens in a coop above a fishpond. The larvae disappear in a scrum of chickens. Nearby, more larvae grow in modified jerrycans, while adult flies are kept in netted boxes. Bikanyale kept chickens before he fled to Uganda from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

stories.title: I was kidnapped and held hostage for 977 days. Could I forgive my captors?
stories.summary: Illustration: Anaïs Mims/Steffan Roth/Roberto Schmidt/Getty/Guardian Design View image in fullscreen Illustration: Anaïs Mims/Steffan Roth/Roberto Schmidt/Getty/Guardian Design I was kidnapped and held hostage for 977 days. At first the idea of mercy was something that helped me through the ordeal. But would real forgiveness be a form of Stockholm syndrome? I knew Mohamed Tahlil as a gentle pirate who oversaw a team of guards during the first months of my life as a hostage in 2012. I had travelled to Somalia to report on the outbreak of modern piracy off the coast.
